arXiv:2508.13281v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Spin defects in two-dimensional materials are a promising platform for quantum sensing. Simulating the defect's optical response and optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast is key to identifying suitable candidates. item.description:

👤 Yousef Mafi, K. G. S. H. Gunawardana, Kim Pöyhönen, Teemu Ojanen
arXiv:2611.09814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When does a quantum particle arrive at a detector? The temporal distributions of itinerant quantum particles have been debated since the birth of quantum mechanics. Here we study the arrival-time problem in periodically monitored spin chains and quantum circuits. The arrival dynamics exhibits two regimes, the quantum Zeno and the low-monitoring regime, separated by an optimal monitoring period set by the single-particle bandwidth. In support of the theory, on superconducting quantum hardware, we measure arrival-time distributions for single and multiple interacting particles in one- and two-dimensional circuits. item.title: Quantum Integration Software Suite For HPC-Quantum Computing Workflows
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Mateusz Meller, Joseph C. R. Thacker, Thomas W. Keal, Vendel Szeremi
arXiv:2611.09659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we focus on addressing challenges related to modelling the integration of conventional high-performance computing (HPC) and quantum computing (QC). We introduce the Quantum Assembly Compiler (QASC) for OpenQASM3.0 files. The compiler produces an executable that leverages the high-performance simulator QuEST to simulate quantum programs. Additionally, we introduce a performance modelling tool, QACC-perf, which can estimate the cost of integrating QC in classical HPC workflows, as well as the execution time of the quantum circuits. Finally, we demonstrate the utility of these tools in the context of multiscale quantum chemistry workflows using the ChemShell computational chemistry environment.

item.title: Sharp error tolerance of the monogamy-of-entanglement game
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Llorenç Escolà-Farràs, Florian Speelman
arXiv:2611.09504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The BB84 monogamy-of-entanglement (MoE) game has numerous applications in quantum cryptography, including quantum key distribution, position verification, and unclonable encryption. In this short note, we improve the error threshold for parallel repetition with identical answer strings from the approximately 3.7% certified by the original bound to the sharp threshold (1-1/sqrt2)/2approx14.64%. When the players need not give identical answers, we also obtain exponential decay whenever the sum of their error tolerances is below this threshold. These bounds strengthen existing security reductions to the BB84 MoE game, improving security bounds and certified noise tolerances for cryptographic protocols.

arXiv:2611.08590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a class of quantum circuits, known as quantum many-body spin ratchets, which act on alternating spin chains with two distinct spin types on even and odd sites. item.title: 一种基于核函数的量子计算态密度估计器
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Julio Cesar Siqueira Rocha
本文提出了一种用于估计量子多体系统态密度（DoS）的量子核方法。该方法利用Rodeo算法作为物理实现，无需修改其标准单辅助比特电路。通过对哈尔随机输入态的Rodeo响应进行平均，可以重建与谱核卷积后的DoS，其中谱核的解析形式完全由采样演化时间的概率分布决定。这建立了经典核多项式方法（KPM）的直接量子模拟，并量化了估计器的统计和系统不确定性。该方法在二维横场自旋-1/2和自旋-1伊辛模型上进行了数值验证。

在NISQ时代，开放量子系统的量子模拟面临耗散动力学的非幺正性和有限量子资源的挑战。本文提出了一种高效的量子算法，用于在NISQ设备上模拟Lindblad动力学。对于具有泡利耗散的开放系统，研究推导了一个紧凑稳定的混合幺正伴随通道，通过轨迹采样实现无辅助比特的耗散动力学近似。为进一步减少电路深度，引入了自适应变分量子轨迹压缩框架，通过训练深度自适应参数化量子电路来近似重复的哈密顿量模拟算符，从而替代采样轨迹中重复的幺正段。

item.title: 线性与高斯量子光学中的轨道维度
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Eliott Z. Mamon
本文研究了给定玻色子态在线性或二次哈密顿量演化下可达到的量子态流形（轨道）的维度。这些拓扑量揭示了可达态空间结构的基本洞察，例如玻色子聚束不会增加可访问方向的数量。研究展示了如何计算轨道维度，并说明其可用于推导某些变换的“不可行”结果。此外，文章提出了利用零差/外差测量或光子计数器探测轨道维度的方法，并将其与玻色子变分电路可访问的方向数联系起来。

在量子计算机上模拟非厄米动力学常受成功概率衰减和非对角化矩阵不稳定性的阻碍。本文提出了基于轮廓矩阵分解（CBMD）的量子泛函演算框架，用于模拟非厄米矩阵函数。CBMD将全纯非厄米算符分解为厄米分量的线性组合，并通过有限截断实现受控误差。对于一阶动力学，CBMD在所有参数上均达到最优查询复杂度，并可推广到二阶波动力学和非厄米特殊函数，显著降低了所需资源。

item.title: Limit cycles in periodically driven open quantum systems
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Paul Menczel, Kay Brandner
arXiv:1908.03900v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the long-time behavior of quantum N-level systems that are coupled to a Markovian environment and subject to periodic driving. As our main result, we obtain a general algebraic condition ensuring that all solutions of a periodic quantum master equation with Lindblad form approach a unique limit cycle. Quite intuitively, this criterion requires that the dissipative terms of the master equation connect all subspaces of the system Hilbert space during an arbitrarily small fraction of the cycle time. Our results provide a natural extension of Spohn's algebraic condition for the approach to equilibrium to systems with external driving.

item.title: Low-rank geometry of two-qubit gates
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Llorenç Balada Gaggioli
arXiv:2604.15102v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a framework based on the determinantal geometry of two-qubit gates. Combining the Weyl chamber representation with operator Schmidt theory, we interpret gate synthesis as a distance problem to determinantal varieties. This gives an operational geometry to the Weyl chamber, quantifying nonlocal complexity. We show that the square root of iSWAP gate is the closest perfect entangler to the variety of local operations, and that no perfect entangler can be approximated by a local gate with average gate fidelity above 78.3%. The three different determinantal costs form a synthesis-adapted coordinate system that encodes nonlocal complexity and generally reconstruct the Weyl coordinates in the reduced sector.
